title: Release-prep must also read lore-cli's CHANGELOG by ref: a breaking marker in either repo forces the pair past a patch bump
description:
QCLI-328 (opum-ai/quest-cli#367, squash bee1636) built the per-repository half of opum-doc ADR gate-release-prep-on-a-breaking-changelog-entry-at-a-patch-bump (Decision paragraph 1). scripts/check-breaking-bump.mjs reads quest's own CHANGELOG only.

The ADR's Consequences paragraph goes further. Lore and quest share one version (constitution Article 3 clause 1), so a breaking marker in EITHER repository's CHANGELOG forces the pair's bump to at least minor. The check must therefore run against both CHANGELOGs before either side's release proceeds. That includes the repository that "did not change functionally" in the release. Today a breaking entry in lore-cli's CHANGELOG would let quest ship the pair at a patch number.

Orchestrator ruling, 2026-09-28, in a cross-session message to quest-cli: KEEP (QCLI-328) did NOT cover this. File it as a follow-up. It slots after QCLI-331 unless the pair release comes first. lore-cli gets the mirror ruling on LCLI-632 AC3. The ADR is the binding record. The message is the routing.

Scope: quest's release-prep also reads lore-cli's CHANGELOG notes for the paired version BY REF, and applies the same marker-vs-patch rule. The ref is lore-cli dev through the GitHub API, or the paired release ref. The notes are `## Unreleased`, or `## <version>` once finalized. The check FAILS CLOSED when lore's CHANGELOG cannot be read.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest's release-prep reads lore-cli's CHANGELOG by ref, through the GitHub API on lore-cli dev or the paired release ref. It applies the same `### ... (breaking)` marker vocabulary and patch-bump rule as scripts/check-breaking-bump.mjs, so a breaking heading in lore's notes for the paired version refuses a patch-level bump of the pair.

When lore's CHANGELOG cannot be read (a 404, an auth failure, a network error, or no parseable version section), the check FAILS with a message naming that cause. It never passes because nothing was read.

Proven as separate measurements on one quest tree: a lore CHANGELOG with a breaking heading refuses the patch bump and accepts a minor bump, and an unreadable lore source refuses. The same run shows the quest-only check unchanged.
The check's output names the lore ref it read and how many lore CHANGELOG sections it read, so a clean result can be told apart from an empty read.

implementationNotes:
Built 2026-09-28 on feat/QCLI-403-cross-changelog-gate (code commit 9fc2524).

WHERE IT RUNS, a design point: NOT in the breaking_bump source gate. That gate is inside the required source-gates context, and the network-read-in-a-required-context ruling (the same one behind QCLI-358) keeps it offline. The quest-only form is unchanged there. The pair form is `--pair` (bun run check:breaking-bump:pair). release.yml runs it right after the version-parity gate and before any npm publish, and the runbook adds a release-prep step: `--pair --lore-ref dev --next <x.y.z>` before the number is chosen. It reads lore main by default, the same ref version-parity reads. Article 3.6 already refuses a unilateral release (parity has no override), so the old unilateral-patch exception cannot reach this gate.

MECHANISM: gh api resolves the ref to a commit sha, then reads CHANGELOG.md at THAT sha, so the answer names exactly what was read. The section parser now accepts lore's Keep a Changelog headings (## [x.y.z] - date, ## [Unreleased]). Quest's own headings parse exactly as before.

EVIDENCE:
- test/qcli403-pair-breaking-bump.test.ts, 6 tests. On one quest tree: lore breaking plus 1.4.0->1.4.1 is refused, 1.4.0->1.5.0 is accepted, and lore clean at the patch is accepted. The finalized ## [x.y.z] section is read once it exists. 404, 401 and network failures each refuse, naming the cause, and a file with no version section refuses. The reader does ref->sha, then reads the file at that sha. The quest-only result is deep-equal with and without --pair, and prepublish runs the quest-only form. release.yml orders parity < pair < npm publish.
- Red before: on the pre-change script the file fails to import (no checkPairBreakingBump export), 0 pass.
- Mutation M1: reverting the heading regex to the unbracketed form. Predicted red: the refuse-patch and finalized tests. Actual: exactly those 2 of 13 (qcli328 plus qcli403).
- Mutation M2: dropping the no-version-section guard. Predicted: only the unreadable test. Actual: exactly that 1 of 13.
- LIVE, against real lore-cli:
  - --pair: quest 0.11.0 (11 sections) and lore 0.11.0 (28 sections) at opum-ai/lore-cli@main (e7f2032), exit 0.
  - --pair --lore-ref dev --next 0.11.1: lore ## [Unreleased] at dev 640195e, no breaking heading, patch, exit 0.
  - --pair --lore-ref no-such-ref-xyz: refused, "No commit found for SHA ... (HTTP 422)", exit 1.
  - quest-only: unchanged output, exit 0.
- bun run check: 902 pass, 0 fail. lore check: 0.
finalSummary: The breaking-bump gate now reads lore-cli CHANGELOG by ref, because the pair shares one version: a breaking heading in lore notes for the paired version refuses a patch-level bump of the pair. check-breaking-bump.mjs --pair resolves the lore ref (main by default, --lore-ref otherwise) to a sha and reads CHANGELOG.md at that sha through the GitHub API. It parses lore bracketed headings, names the ref, sha and section count it read, and fails closed on any unreadable or version-less file. release.yml runs it beside version-parity, before the publish. The quest-only source gate is unchanged and offline. Verified: 6 new tests; red-before; two predicted-subset mutations exact (2/13, 1/13); live runs against lore main and dev plus a bad ref; bun run check 902/0; lore check 0.
